structured_output.analysis: iso_3.15 sits exactly at the budget. For the six retrieved layers, it already uses the lowest-KL method at each layer's current bit tier, and all tabled moves have small positive predicted deltas. Single-layer swaps therefore look exhausted, so this round tests the untried GPTQ option axes. Measured KL (0.4361) exceeds the single-layer prediction (0.3983), so interactions matter and the predictions are only a rough guide. Three proposals change one option each with no bit change. The fourth tries weight.group_size=256 on all GPTQ-family methods to free metadata bits for six upgrades on loss-concentrated layers. Its bit saving is my estimate from the per-weight deltas, not a measured figure, and the KL effect of the larger group size is unmeasured.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Base iso_3.15 measured KL 0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e] with default options. Loss-concentrated layers show heavy-tailed activations, such as activation kurtosis 1090.09 [E24beed188b6a] and activation channel_absmax_ratio 65.2425 [E3c29dce14bae] on model.layers.27.mlp.up_proj. This tests weight_algo.act_order=true on all GPTQ-family methods with no layer changes.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_damp_high
proposals.rationale: Base iso_3.15 measured validation KL 0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e], while the layer table comes from a calibration run. Stronger damping may reduce dependence on outlier activations, such as activation absmax 520.657 [E17ce1bbeaa4a] on model.layers.27.mlp.up_proj. This tests weight_algo.damp=0.05 with no layer changes.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_damp_low
proposals.rationale: This is the opposite direction to the high-damping grid, testing weight_algo.damp=0.002 from base iso_3.15, which measured KL 0.43614466651129274 [E514ab09c524e]. Weaker damping leaves more of the measured activation structure in the compensation, for example activation channel_absmax_ratio 30.6919 [E907421e288cc] on model.layers.2.mlp.up_proj. There are no layer changes.
